close_reason: Fixed in a07804b: applied option 2 (doc-only) matching the canonical Email.mailbox_ids precedent. Rationale: option 1 (typed wrapper like HashMap<Id, ()>) would (a) diverge from the workspace canonical pattern, (b) break the PatchObject 'null = remove' semantics that share the same map shape, and (c) require a broader sweep across Email.mailbox_ids, Email.keywords, and every similar field. Added rustdoc on address_book_ids, members, and keywords explaining the MUST-be-true contract and pointing handler authors (jmap-contacts-server) at the invalidProperties rejection path. Added 3 deserialise-cleanly tests pinning the type's permissive contract.
description:
RFC 9610 §3 says `addressBookIds` is `Id[Boolean]` "the set of AddressBook
ids this card belongs to. Each value MUST be true." RFC 9553 §2.1.6 says
the same for `members` (group membership): "The keys are the URIs of the
member entities, and each value MUST be true."

Current types (crate-jmap-contacts-types/src/card.rs:43,65) accept any bool:

```rust
pub address_book_ids: Option<HashMap<Id, bool>>,
pub members:          Option<HashMap<String, bool>>,
```

A caller (server or client) inserting `false` produces a card that
deserializes / serializes cleanly but violates the wire-format contract.
Backends that match membership / containment by truthiness silently
disagree across implementations.

The Rust type doesn't model the "set" intent — `HashMap<Id, bool>` is
the wrong shape for "a set". Two acceptable resolutions:

1. Typed wrapper. Introduce a `pub struct IdSet(HashSet<Id>)` (or
   `MemberSet`) with a custom serde adapter that emits `{id: true}` and
   accepts `{id: true}` only. Makes `false` unrepresentable; wire format
   identical for valid input.

2. Doc-only fix. Add a rustdoc clause stating "each map value MUST be
   `true` per RFC 9610 §3 / RFC 9553 §2.1.6; servers MAY reject `false`
   with InvalidArguments." Still forces every caller to write the
   validation themselves, but at least documents the contract.

This is a contract that callers cannot satisfy correctly without
writing the validation themselves. Defensive-code-forcing on every
consumer.

References:
- RFC 9610 §3 addressBookIds field
- RFC 9553 §2.1.6 members field
- Compare: jmap-types Id-set helpers (if any)
title: ContactCard.addressBookIds and members allow value=false; spec requires MUST true
